clue.text: That's three times European upset sensitive person

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European, taken three times

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a delicate soul has been upset by Europeans three times over.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of THATS plus EEE, rearranged as 'upset' signals, give the answer; the apostrophe adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An aesthete is a person especially attuned to beauty and art, hence sensitive in taste.

clue.text: Stops and takes a breather after a run

indicators.note: after puts the breather behind the run in the answer

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
to take a breather is to rest

explanation.surface: Someone halts and pauses for breath after going for a jog.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrests means halts or checks, as in arresting a decline.

clue.text: He, for example, symbolically raised flag here

indicators.note: in a down answer raised means read upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: He is the chemical symbol of helium, which is a gas

explanation.surface: A man hoisted the flag at this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' poses as a man raising a flag, but it is helium; 'here' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to droop or tire, the same as to sink or slump.

clue.text: Political body's outstanding, preoccupied with domestic issues

parts.note: a house is a legislative chamber, such as the House of Commons
proud can mean projecting, standing out from a surface

explanation.surface: A parliament is praised as excellent while busy with home affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'domestic issues' suggests national policy, but it means housework.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone house-proud is fussy about keeping their home clean and tidy.

clue.text: Subject gets to choose when king is finally expelled

indicators.note: expelled means thrown out, and finally places the lost letter at the end

parts.note: to pick is to choose
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A citizen gets to make the choice once the monarch has at last been thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a subject of discussion or writing.

clue.text: Dog entertained in broadcast

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to broadcast seed is to sow it
had (guests) means entertained them

explanation.surface: A dog was featured on a broadcast programme.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow them closely, the verb sense of trailing a person unseen.

clue.text: Philosopher, not good-hearted, unpleasant type

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter is taken away

parts.note: Hegel was a German philosopher
G for good, the letter at the heart of the philosopher's name

explanation.surface: A philosopher who lacks kindness is a nasty piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good-hearted' reads as kindly, but it is G, the middle letter of HEGEL, removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A heel is a contemptible, untrustworthy person, a cad.

clue.text: Doing cuts in, in a way?

definitions.text: Doing cuts in, in a way?

parts.words: Doing cuts in, in a way?
parts.note: making reductions in price, and also counting someone out rather than in

explanation.surface: Someone is interrupting by cutting in, after a fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Discounting means reducing a price, making a cut, and also disregarding or ruling something out.

clue.text: No play, with cast being idle

parts.note: from the saying all work and no play, work is the opposite of play
to shy is to throw or cast

explanation.surface: An actor with no part in the play, cast aside, is idle.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone work-shy avoids labour, so is lazy.

clue.text: Trouble in which Marat fatally found himself

definitions.meaning: to be in a fix or a scrape

definitions.text: in which Marat fatally found himself
definitions.meaning: the revolutionary Marat was stabbed in his bath by Charlotte Corday

explanation.surface: A French revolutionary met a deadly predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a predicament is a common idiom for being in difficulty, and Marat literally died bathing.

clue.text: Distinguished academic — one in four progresses improperly

indicators.note: improperly means not in the correct way, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A distinguished scholar complains that one in four students progresses improperly.
explanation.walkthrough: I with FOUR and PROGRESSES, fifteen letters, are rearranged as 'improperly' signals; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Regius chair is a royally founded professorship at old British universities, so its holder is an eminent academic.

clue.text: Badly scared by bullies — they are above criticism

indicators.note: badly means in a poor or wrong way, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: to cow someone is to intimidate or bully them

explanation.surface: People frightened by bullies are said to be beyond reproach.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred cow is an idiom for an institution or idea treated as immune from challenge.

clue.text: Cold, wrapped in friend's furs

indicators.note: wrapped in means enclosed by, so the cold goes inside the friend's

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so friend's is CHINAS
a chill is a coldness

explanation.surface: Someone cold wraps up in a friend's fur coats.
explanation.walkthrough: China plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinchilla pelts are prized soft furs from small South American rodents.

clue.text: Rings Police Sergeant, giving statement after accident

parts.note: rings are round shapes, each like the letter O

explanation.surface: A police sergeant phones someone to give a statement after a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rings' looks like a telephone call and 'statement' like a police report, but the statement is the exclamation one makes after a slip.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation of dismay someone utters after a small mishap, a spoken remark rather than a report.

clue.text: Person petitioning to replace over one hundred

indicators.note: over here means covering, so the replacing word surrounds the rest

parts.note: to supplant is to replace
one is the Roman numeral I
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A petitioner asks to replace more than a hundred people.
explanation.definitionFit: A supplicant is someone humbly begging or asking for something.

clue.text: Small thing needed in hearing to get Republican excited

indicators.note: to get someone excited is to stir them up, so Republican goes inside that phrase

parts.note: excited here stands for stir up, to rouse or agitate

explanation.surface: A small item needed at a court hearing is used to rile a Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To get Republican excited' is 'to stir Republican up': R sits between STIR and UP. 'Hearing' suggests a court, but it is the sense of hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: The stapes is a tiny stirrup-shaped bone of the middle ear that passes sound vibrations inward.

clue.text: Yearly cost for housing of some older relatives

parts.note: PA is per annum, by the year
a rental is the sum paid to rent a home

explanation.surface: The annual price of housing elderly relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Parental means relating to mothers and fathers, the generation above you.

clue.text: Some foreign money's returned after trip, old sport

indicators.note: after puts the money behind the trip in the answer

parts.note: a tour is a trip

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the money is read backwards

parts.note: the yen is the currency of Japan

explanation.surface: After a trip abroad, some foreign currency is handed back to an old sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old sport' looks like a friendly address to a man, but it is a medieval jousting contest; YEN reversed gives NEY.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourney was a medieval tournament of knights jousting, an old sporting contest.

clue.text: Put finishing touches to a clue concocted about queen and king

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters wrap around the queen
concocted means made up, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: R is for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A setter puts finishing touches to a clue invented about royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put finishing touches to' sounds like polishing the clue itself, but it defines the act of varnishing; R for king comes from Latin rex.
explanation.definitionFit: To varnish a surface with a hard glossy coat is to give it its final finish.

clue.text: With a number of Germans around area, one's cooperated

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the German song wraps the rest

parts.note: a lied is a German song, a number
one is I, and 's is is, giving IS

explanation.surface: Joining a crowd of Germans gathered round an area, one collaborated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' looks like a count, but it is a song: a German lied.
explanation.definitionFit: To liaise is to work together and keep in contact, so liaised means worked jointly.

clue.text: One short answer after another, enclosing carbon copy

indicators.note: after places the one and another answer behind the shortened reply

parts.note: a reply is an answer; short means its last letter is dropped

indicators.note: enclosing means surrounding, so the pair goes round the carbon

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
another answer, abbreviated A
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: Answers come one after another, each with a carbon copy attached.
explanation.walkthrough: REPLY loses its Y; then I and A (a further answer) close round C.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is an exact reproduction of an original, the same thing as a duplicate.

clue.text: Ace and ten, perhaps, to be deliberately played

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

indicators.note: perhaps means possibly in some other form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A card player lays down the ace and the ten slowly and on purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ace and ten' suggests cards, but an ante is the stake put up before a hand; 'to be' is a link and the definition is a tempo marking.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is a musical direction for a moderate, walking tempo, unhurried playing.

clue.text: Political alliance creating a boundary towards West

indicators.note: in an across answer reading towards the west means right to left, so the word is reversed

parts.note: in cricket a six is a boundary, a hit clearing the rope

explanation.surface: A political alliance establishes a frontier running westward.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a boundary is a shot reaching the field's edge, scoring four or six runs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Axis was the wartime alliance of Germany, Italy and Japan, a bloc of nations.

clue.text: Like irreconcilable differences about article published in full

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the article goes inside

parts.note: differences that cannot be reconciled are gaps never bridged
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A book about divorce by irreconcilable differences was published in its entirety.
explanation.definitionFit: An unabridged edition is a complete text with nothing cut, so it is printed whole.

clue.text: One enters pub before noon for a tot of Scotch

indicators.note: before puts the pub piece ahead of noon
enters means goes into, so one goes inside the pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A man walks into a pub before midday for a dram of whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot of Scotch' suggests a measure of whisky, but it is a Scottish small child.
explanation.definitionFit: Bairn is the Scots word for a child, a little one.

clue.text: Old boys going to university-list of available courses

parts.note: old boys are grown men

explanation.surface: Former pupils going on to university are given the prospectus of courses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courses' suggests degree courses, but they are courses of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu lists the dishes a restaurant serves, the courses one may order.

clue.text: Test in which one cannot be replaced by substitute

definitions.text: Test in which one cannot be replaced by substitute

parts.words: Test in which one cannot be replaced by substitute
parts.note: an exam in which one examines oneself, so no one else can sit it for you

explanation.surface: An exam where no stand-in candidate is allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Introspective scrutiny of one's own conduct is a test only oneself can carry out.

clue.text: Accommodation that's seen between German and Austrian banks

definitions.meaning: a pub or small hotel offering rooms

definitions.text: that's seen between German and Austrian banks
definitions.meaning: the River ... forms part of the German-Austrian border, flowing between banks in each country

explanation.surface: Lodging spotted on the border between German and Austrian banks.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a hostelry giving lodging, and the Inn is a river on the German-Austrian border.

clue.text: Record set by American in athletics event

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
US means American

explanation.surface: An American sets a record in an athletics event.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing the discus is a field event in athletics meetings.

clue.text: Contemporary attitude, for example

parts.note: in means fashionable, of the moment
a stance is a position or attitude

explanation.surface: A modern outlook is cited as a typical case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for example' looks like a single phrase, but 'for' is a link and 'example' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a particular case cited to illustrate something.
